class: Any identifier built for one channel from the limit of a different channel of the same vendor (the API order tag allows 20 characters, the Publisher basket page allows 8) exceeds the stricter channel's limit once a counter inside it grows a digit, so the feature works for the first nine entities and fails for every one after.
mechanism: make_tag (backend/ofo/execution/basket.py:89-97) allows 20 characters and builds OFS{s}V{v}L{i}; Kite's basket page (Kite Publisher /connect/basket) refuses a tag over 8 characters, so any strategy id >= 10 (strategy 11 -> OFS11V1L0) or version >= 10 (OFS9V10L0 is 9) is refused.

first_seen.where: GC-3L live entry on the owner's Kite account, strategy 11
first_seen.evidence: Kite returned {"status":"error","message":"`tag` should be max 8 characters","error_type":"InputException"}; Kite Orders: "You haven't placed any orders today" (nothing placed); every user's 10th strategy onward cannot execute; workaround: the same leg on strategy 9 (tag OFS9V1L0, 8 chars) filled

fix: Not fixed. Class fix: one tag builder whose limit is the minimum across the basket page and the API (8), covering entry and exit tags and versions >= 10, with a test that fails on any generated tag over 8 characters for large ids; the tag lookup used for reconciliation (ADR-054) must still resolve the shorter form.

detection.note: Found only by a live basket on strategy id 11. Discrimination to prove when built: OFS9V1L0 passes, OFS11V1L0 and OFS9V10L0 fail the length check today. Unmeasured: Kite's rule on allowed characters.

occurrences.evidence: InputException: `tag` should be max 8 characters; no order placed
